Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

anything pronoun

no matter what

also anything at all, whatever you like, anything you like, whatever! (I don’t care)

classical

Plaut. Truc. 4.4.31: dīcere hīc quidvīs licet (Lewis & Short)
Ter. Heaut. 4.1.28: quidvīs satis est (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 406

quidvīs

pronoun (neuter of quīvīs)

anything you like, anything whatever

As an adjective, quīvīs, quaevīs, quodvīs: quōvīs modō, in any way at all (Sall. J. 11.9, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • quidlibet — anything at all, whatever comes

    pronoun (neuter of quīlibet) · also used · classical · Hor. Ars 9–10 (Lewis & Short); Hor. S. 1.9.12–13: cum quidlibet ille garrīret (Lewis & Short)

    Often a little slighting: just anything, the first thing that comes (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • pictōribus atque poētīs quidlibet audendī semper fuit aequa potestās

    painters and poets have always had an equal right to dare anythingHor. Ars 9–10

  • Quidvīs!

    Whatever!Traupman 406

See also anything, something.

SourcesLewis & Short: quivis · Lewis & Short: quilibet

Horace quoted as Lewis & Short cites him (s.v. quilibet: A. P. 9).
